urls.title: Leafy Goose: A Human-Led AI Assistant for Maintainers’ Community Work

data.text:
Maintainers, how often do you answer the same onboarding questions? 

@anajsana95 created Leafy Goose which uses goose and your community guide to draft Discord replies. 

Here's how to adapt it for your community 👇
https://t.co/bjYavRV2ee

Minimal by design. 235 tokens and still getting the job done.

Lowest context tax in the chart, leaving more room for you to work. https://t.co/o0AezeDR04

urls.description: I asked Goose “how are you?” and it took 14 seconds to answer. That got me wondering: why did it take so long? Was it the model? The network? The agent itself? I decided to try and find out. Goose has built-in OpenTelemetry support, so it was easy enough to wire it up to Jaeger for distributed tracing. I also added ClickHouse so the traces would survive a restart. Stack My stack consisted of three components:
urls.title: Trace and Analyse Goose Sessions with OpenTelemetry, Jaeger and ClickHouse

data.text:
What's taking so long in your goose session? 🔍

Vikram Vaswani shows how to use goose's built-in OpenTelemetry support to inspect model and tool calls in Jaeger, with ClickHouse keeping traces around after a restart.

https://t.co/DMj6a1sjs4

urls.description: Uncle Bob stopped reading the code his agents write and replaced review with deterministic tools. That works on one laptop. Here is how to build the same gauntlet for a team, with goose, MCP and agentgateway, so no agent can skip a check.
urls.title: I'm with Uncle Bob. But only if nobody can skip the checks

data.text:
"Done" needs a passing check. 

Antonio Berben walks through a goose workflow with complexity checks, mutation testing, and architecture rules. Recipes retry failed checks, while agentgateway controls which MCP checker each agent can access.

https://t.co/tEJAkl5COI https://t.co/AHiAVWiUbM

urls.title: Making Decisions with Jev and Goose | Vidya

data.text:
Curious about Jev? Plug the new decision model into Goose 🪿

This walkthrough shows how to connect them with an Agent Skill and put Jev to work making decisions in your workflow.

@nnennahacks shows how to add permission checks through MCP, including why you need to check which other enabled tools can write to those same files.

Read the walkthrough
https://t.co/qefM3dcDJM

urls.description: A tour of Goose, from adding MCP tools to changing how the agent works.
urls.title: What you can change when your agent is open source

data.text:
Make goose work the way your team does 🪿

@onlydole walks through adding MCP tools and deciding when to change the agent itself, using lint checks as a practical example.

Start small, customize what you need 👇
https://t.co/YmWb5GEYd5

urls.description: Using Goose to create re-usable and shareable prompts
urls.title: Intro to Goose Recipes and Sub-Recipes

data.text:
Goose recipes let you save and share reusable workflows. Subrecipes split larger workflows into smaller steps.

Adriana Villela explains both with a Kubernetes example and shares the issues she hit along the way. 

https://t.co/2pTQnghhkj https://t.co/JiwxbudxR7

note_tweet.text:
Multi-cloud Kubernetes inventory sounds simple… until you add an AI agent to the mix. 🪿

@pavanmadduri27 shares a reference design for using goose to collect Kubernetes inventory from OKE and AKS.

The design uses read-only cloud credentials and human approval, so the model can coordinate the work without controlling access.

https://t.co/buBdaw3CF8

data.text:
A Goose walks into an enterprise Java stack… 🪿☕

In Part 1 of this new tutorial, @danieloh30 shows how to build cloud-native MCP tool services with Quarkus LangChain4j, add Jakarta Bean Validation, and connect them to Goose over HTTP.

Honk responsibly: https://t.co/AZ8KZ8vVsV

One interface, no tabs needed. You shouldn't have to think about if you're coding or working or... wait, how are those even different?

Just tell Goose what you want to do and it'll figure the rest out. https://t.co/JO47xMtG00
